Response to guidelines 4.3 and 4.2.6 — Part 1 of 2

Hello App Review,

Thank you for the opportunity to clarify TapLead’s purpose and development.

1. Function and primary problem

TapLead helps users retain the context of professional introductions and act on them afterward. Users create a digital card, share its published profile through a QR code or link, and maintain connection records containing meeting context, notes, tags, relationship status and a follow-up date. A connection’s timeline records notes and follow-up actions; the Today screen surfaces due follow-ups. The problem it addresses is losing the context and next action after exchanging contact details.

2. Intended audience

TapLead is intended for individual professionals who manage their own networking relationships: independent consultants, freelancers, founders and people attending professional events. Its workflow is designed around the person conducting the conversation and managing the subsequent follow-up.

3. Market need and differentiation

We acknowledge that digital cards, contact notes and tags already exist in this category. We do not claim to have invented those features. TapLead’s intended distinction is its integrated, individual-focused workflow: retain meeting context, review or edit notes, explicitly schedule the next action, and revisit that action alongside the connection’s history. It includes native reminders, QR widgets and App Shortcuts. Users review introduction drafts themselves; TapLead does not automatically send messages or mark a relationship as contacted merely because a draft was created.

4. Beta testing and changes

Testing has been developer-led through TestFlight, with automated tests supplementing physical-device checks. We have not conducted a broad external beta or collected a larger body of customer feedback.

The developer reported successful purchase and restore testing on an iPhone for build 1015. Your subsequent iPad review exposed a missing or expired-session path that those checks had missed. Build 1016 separates StoreKit product loading from account authentication and adds direct sign-in recovery and retry handling. The developer then confirmed successful purchase and Restore Purchases on a physical iPad running iPadOS 26.7. Separate automated regression tests passed on iPhone and iPad simulators. The subscription correction followed App Review feedback; we do not represent it as feedback from external beta users.

Response to guidelines 4.3 and 4.2.6 — Part 2 of 2

5. Standalone product or suite

TapLead is our own standalone product, with our own concept and branding. It is not a client-specific variant or part of a suite of related networking apps. No other app on our developer account shares its contact/networking functionality.

6. Consolidation with another app

There is no other app on our developer account with a shared contact/networking workflow into which TapLead would naturally fit as an in-app purchase or feature expansion. Its cards, connections, meeting context and follow-up history form a coherent standalone product.

7. Shared components with our other apps

No other app on our developer account shares TapLead’s code or artwork. Its widget extension belongs to TapLead and is distributed with the same app.

8. Shared components with third-party apps

TapLead is implemented as a native SwiftUI project with a local TapLeadCore package for its domain models and supporting logic. We used AI-assisted coding tools during development. We did not adopt a third-party app codebase, white-label application or commercial application template. Standard platform and server libraries support functions such as authentication, networking and subscription verification; they do not supply TapLead’s application screens or networking workflow.

9. Client or third-party ownership

TapLead was not created for a client, partner or third party supplying the concept, content or branding. We own and operate the product and submit it directly through our developer account.

Please reconsider the submission using these clarifications. If a particular screen, asset or workflow prompted the template or duplication concern, please identify it so we can address it specifically.
status: Both parts posted and read back in App Store Connect
